correctness.rationale: For n>=5 in the simple cubic graph GP(n,2), both binary colour classes are total dominating iff both specified open-neighborhood triples are nonmonochromatic. An exact 256-state four-column transfer T with 576 transitions counts all named cyclic binary assignments by tr(T^n). Independently reconstructed T, computed exact integer traces n=1..256, and applied Newton identities to all 256 coefficients of det(I-zT), recovering the stated degree-64 product (1-z^2)^4(1-2z^2-z^6)(1+2z^4-z^6)P20 P24, including all zero tail coefficients. Direct independent bit-vector enumeration for n=5..9 confirmed A_n=12,116,226,1286,2486, while the trace yields n=5..14 values exactly as claimed. Three-colour validity means every 3-vertex open neighborhood has all three colours; a 6th-order linear recurrence over F3 has characteristic factor dividing t^30-1. Independently exhausted all 729 initial sextuples modulo 3 over a complete forced 30-period and found precisely six valid named affine period-three colourings, one unordered partition iff 3|n. Cubic degree excludes >=4 classes. All-order claims follow from the exact determinant and finite-period proof, not extrapolating the first counts.

originality.rationale: Earlier Zelinka total-domatic number and Minyard–Sepanski Theorem 4.2 establish qualitative existence of three total-domination classes for GP(n,2) iff 3|n; neither gives the complete two-class counting series. Zhao et al. 2020 concerns minimum total dominating sets, not all partitions; Choi et al. 2026 concerns 2-coupon existence/constraints for cubic graphs. The three-class EXISTENCE criterion is a covered result and is explicitly credited; uniqueness and especially the new exact degree-64 two-class trace enumerator are the surviving claim. No equivalent count was found in Resultary or checked papers; specialized unindexed counting tables remain a risk.
residual_risks: A specialized older 2-coupon counting transfer matrix or graph colouring database may already imply the exact binary generating function.
The published three-colour existence classification is not new; value is in exact multiplicities and full enumerator.
The finite determinant identity is verified computationally and relies on a 256-state exact certificate, not a conceptual small spectral decomposition.
